verdict.rationale: iTerm2's documented AppleScript support lets you write stand-alone scripts that launch the app and open multiple sessions with profiles in new tabs or windows. An AutoLaunch.scpt runs at startup, and a Python API offers full automation, so a project workspace can be scripted to open in one go. However, the evidence never shows split-pane layouts being created from a script, and it shows no declarative config for saved window layouts, so the layout part of the story is only implied. Missing for 10: documented scripted or config-defined pane/split layouts, saved window arrangements in config, and hands-on corroboration of a one-command project workspace.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can define startup sessions and window layouts in config or scripts so a project workspace opens in one command

citations.quote: iTerm2 has sophisticated AppleScript support allowing one to write stand-alone scripts to launch the application and open multiple sessions with profiles into either new tabs or new windows.
On startup, iTerm2 looks for an AppleScript file in "~/Library/Application Support/iTerm2/Scripts/AutoLaunch.scpt". If it is found, the "AutoLaunch.scpt" script is launched and executed.
Python Scripting API - Full automation and customization via Python.
